title: Merck and Moderna's Phase 3 INTerpath-001 Trial Meets Primary Endpoint — First Randomized Phase 3 Confirmation That a Personalized mRNA Cancer Vaccine Works
detail: Merck and Moderna announced that the Phase 3 INTerpath-001 trial of intismeran autogene (mRNA-4157/V940), a personalized neoantigen mRNA cancer vaccine, plus Keytruda (pembrolizumab) met its primary endpoint of recurrence-free survival (RFS) and key secondary endpoint of distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS) versus Keytruda alone, in 1,137 patients with completely resected stage IIB-IV cutaneous melanoma. The companies called the improvements "statistically significant and clinically meaningful" but did not disclose specific hazard ratios or percentage risk reductions, saying detailed data will be presented at an upcoming medical meeting; no new safety signals were observed. INTerpath-001 is the first randomized Phase 3 trial ever designed to definitively prove the benefit of a personalized neoantigen vaccine, following earlier positive Phase 2b KEYNOTE-942 data (49% RFS risk reduction, 59% DMFS risk reduction at 5-year follow-up) that the FDA had previously declined to accelerate-approve on. The vaccine targets up to 34 patient-specific tumor-associated antigens. Merck and Moderna said they now plan to engage regulators on a filing submission, with larger trials already underway in non-small cell lung cancer and mid-stage studies in bladder, kidney, pancreatic, and stomach cancers.

title: MIT Koch Institute Unveils Sugar-Based CAR-T Cryopreservation That Could Expand Access Beyond the 5% of US Hospitals That Can Currently Deliver It
detail: Researchers at MIT's Koch Institute for Integrative Cancer Research (postdocs Amy Lee and Khanh Tran, senior author Robert Langer, principal investigator Ana Jaklenec) published in Trends in Biotechnology a new cryopreservation method for CAR-T cells that uses naturally occurring sugars — trehalose and sucrose, the same antifreeze compounds found in cold-tolerant organisms like wood frogs — instead of relying primarily on DMSO, a toxic solvent that must be carefully removed before infusion. The sugars are loaded into cells via electroporation, briefly opening pores in the cell membrane. In mouse models of lymphoma and glioblastoma, sugar-preserved CAR-T cells showed improved post-thaw survival and antitumor activity versus conventionally DMSO-preserved cells. Because DMSO removal is a complex process most hospitals cannot perform, only about 5% of US hospitals currently have the infrastructure to deliver CAR-T therapy; the researchers say cells preserved this way could theoretically be thawed and injected directly, removing a major access bottleneck.

media.caption: MIT researchers use sugar-based antifreeze compounds to preserve CAR-T cells without toxic DMSO, aiming to expand hospital access to the therapy
